questions.question: Why did Peter write a special letter to Amy and not to his other friends?
questions.explanation: This question checks children’s understanding of what makes Amy’s invitation special, helping them notice ways we can make someone feel special.

questions.question: How did Peter feel when he thought about what his other friends might say about inviting Amy to the party?
questions.explanation: This helps children recognize Peter’s feelings and relate to the worry of doing something kind when others might not agree.

questions.question: Have you ever wanted to invite someone to your party or game when other friends didn’t want you to? What did you do?
questions.explanation: This encourages children to connect the story to their own experiences and think about including others, supporting the moral of friendship and inclusion.

questions.question: How do you think Amy felt when Peter bumped into her and grabbed the letter? What could Peter have done to make her feel better?
questions.explanation: This helps children consider others’ feelings and understand how actions (even accidents) can affect someone, deepening empathy.

questions.question: What happened at the party when Amy arrived? How did everyone act? Why do you think it’s nice that everyone was together?
questions.explanation: This checks recall about the happy ending and opens discussion about the joy of being together and making everyone feel welcome.

questions.question: If you see someone sitting alone or feeling sad, what could you do to help them feel included?
questions.explanation: Children are prompted to take the lesson of inclusiveness and apply it to real life, practicing being kind to others.

questions.question: Do you think it’s okay to be friends with everyone, even if your friends are different from you? Why or why not?
questions.explanation: This question builds understanding that friendships can be with anyone and celebrates differences, linking to the story’s moral.

questions.question: Can you think of a nice thing you could do to make a friend feel special, like Peter did for Amy?
questions.explanation: Children are invited to brainstorm kind actions, showing how they can put the moral into practice.

questions.question: Why shouldn’t we worry too much about what other people say when we want to include someone or be kind?
questions.explanation: This question gets children thinking about the importance of kindness over peer pressure, reinforcing the story’s deeper moral.

questions.question: What do you think Peter might wish for at the end of the story? What would you wish for if all your friends were together with you?
questions.explanation: Encourages children to imagine the joy of friendship and sharing good times, connecting personally to the positive ending.

moral: It is nice to make your friends feel special, and it’s important not to worry too much about what others might say. Everybody can be friends and celebrate together.
learning_objectives: Children will be able to identify ways to make friends feel special.
Children will understand that it’s okay to include everyone, even if others don't agree.
Children will practice thinking about other people's feelings.
Children will be encouraged to make kind choices in their own lives.
discussion_points: Why is it important to make our friends feel special?
How can we be a good friend to someone who feels left out?
What would you do if your friends didn't agree with your choice to invite someone new?
How can we celebrate together, even if we are all different?
When was a time you felt happy to be included by others?
